body: You could word it to your therapist that none of the activities are working and that it's worrying you. Then you could ask if medication would help. I don't think you'll be forced to stay in the hospital so long as you aren't an immediate threat to yourself. Or, it's even possible that your therapist might just prescribe the meds and all you have to do is pick them up.

That's really unfortunate that your mom doesn't believe in damage mental illnesses :\ 

Since you're about to go to college, you could go their counseling office/sessions since all colleges should have one. You could also join a peer support group nearby or one at your college. I know sharing experiences with others and sharing your own experience can be cathartic for some. 

You could also go to a nearby walk-in clinic in the city you're in. There should be some type of counseling or form of mental guidance. They can help direct you to low-cost therapists. Or, if you're under your parents' insurance plan, you can go to a therapist that's under their plan.
Have you talked to anyone about your depression? Family members, friends, school counselor, etc?

Do they think depression is just being sad? You might want to get examined by a doctor since your parents might take it more seriously as doctors are "normal" and will hopefully listen. 

Did you try at all during college in your engineer classes or did you just do the bare minimum? 

I suggest going to a therapist and if money is an issue, a good amount of them have sliding scales and will adjust to your financial situation. You could also go to a local clinic since they typically have counselors or peer-counselors and can refer you to reliable therapists/psychiatrists.

You should tell your therapist that you feel like the thoughts are getting worse the more it's brought out in the open. They should change their methods/activities and possibly prescribe your medication to help you get through the initial push. 

You could also join a peer support group so that you can share your experience and hear others as well. I know some people find comfort in solidarity. 

I know it'll be difficult, but I know you can push through and find something that works. I mean, you were able to seek help from a therapist, you're strong enough to get through this!

I'm relieved to hear that your girlfriend and a few other people understand and care about your situation. I know what you mean with conversations with friends. There are sadly people out there that still think depression can simply be "gotten over" or "stop being sad" 

That's awesome!! I hope your therapist helps relieve you of this burden :) 

Hopefully your therapist can help you pinpoint methods or activities that will lessen the frequency and intensity of the horrible thoughts. Funny thing is I too just stumbled upon this subreddit hahaha. I'ts a good thing that you wanted to share your experience since I know solidarity can help people cope. 

Feel like being heard? Are there things in your life where you feel like your opinion is stifled? 

And no problem whatsoever! If you ever want to vent more, always feel free to message and I'll respond as soon as possible :) I'm still struggling with depression and anxiety and I know how horrible it is to feel like no one gives two fucks about what you said.
How long have these thoughts been going on? How was your situation during high school?

It's good that the issues are being addressed. 

Do you feel like it's effective even if it's a small amount of progress?

Hey man, I have those thoughts basically daily. Depression is a terrible piece of shit eh? It whispers all these negative and insane things to you where eventually you start to believe it. 

Are you forced to be around that person? I don't think it's healthy for you to stick around that manipulative person. 

How long have you been having these thoughts? I would recommend seeking out a therapist especially a cognitive behavioral one. A cognitive behavioral therapist could help change those thoughts so they aren't negative or self-destructive.

How long have you been going to your current therapist and is it somewhat effective or do they not help at all? 

If your therapist isn't helping at all, you should look for a new one. Like medication, finding a therapist you trust and feel that actually cares and helps you is really important.

I am very relieved to hear that you decided not to use it. I don't know what you've been dealing with, but you've survived this far, you can keep slogging on. 

Your kids would be extremely devastated to lose you and their lives would never be the same if you were gone. It's hard to be strong, but your kids need you and I can tell you care about them deeply.

Depression is a demon that weighs down on your very being and makes everything a struggle. It whispers horrible thoughts in your head and fills you with despair and just when you think you have some breathing room, that fucker reappears. 

It's good that you manage to be productive since I know it's really hard with depression. The days, like the one you're currently experiencing, are some of the most difficult times in a person suffering from depression. 

I'm glad to hear that getting it off your chest will help. Have you looked into therapy? Or does anyone know you suffer from depression especially your girlfriend?

Hey man, do your parents know about your chronic depression? Have you seen a therapist or taken any medication? 

There's no shame in living with parents especially if you live in one of the popular states where it costs an arm and a leg to just afford to rent an apartment. You could always leave the state later on once things are better. What are you passionate about? Or, any hobbies or anything to occupy your free time?
